answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 15 for each account already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The comet multiplier is published, charged in ripple, and ocean lists each payment. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 3397 identities would post 1505 proofs and burn roughly 49 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
